title: Invariant-normalized cyclic row comparison with residual action
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism and $\tau=u(1)$. Write $L_J^G$ for trivial-$J$ inflation and $\Gamma_J^G$ for its invariant-inclusion-normalized right adjoint, retaining $G$, for $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. Let $V=\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}$, $U_J:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ and $U_0:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$ forget $G$. Write $Q$ for ordinary derived localization and $\alpha^G_{J,P}:Q\Gamma_J^G P\to R\Gamma_J^G(QP)$ for its canonical computation unit on bounded-below complexes. For a bounded-below $G\times\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$-complex $N$, let $K^G(N)^n=N^n\oplus N^{n-1}$, with $d(x,y)=(d_Nx,(T-1)x-d_Ny)$, where $T$ is the action of $1\in\mathbf Z$, and let $b_N:\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G N\to K^G(N)$ be $(\mathrm{inclusion},0)$. For every injective module $I$ in $\mathcal A_{G\times\mathbf Z}(R)$ the row augmentation $\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G I[0]\to K^G(I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every bounded-below termwise injective complex $I$, the assembled augmentation $b_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. There is a unique natural transformation
$$\theta^G:R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G\longrightarrow QK^G,\qquad \theta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,P}=Q(b_P)$$
on every bounded-below complex $P$, and it is invertible. Its inverse $\lambda^G$ is compatible with canonical shifts and cone boundaries, using the signed total structure of [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated]. For every quasi-isomorphism $a:N\to I$ to a bounded-below injective complex it has the resolution formula
$$\lambda^G_{QN}=(R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(Qa))^{-1}\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,I}Q(b_I)^{-1}Q(K^G a).$$
This formula is independent of the chosen resolution, is natural on diagrams of specified resolutions and their cones, and on a single module has the invariant-inclusion normalization.

Forgetting $G$ leaves $K,b$ and their differentials unchanged. Under the computation-unit-normalized isomorphism $D(U_0)R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G\cong R\Gamma_{R,\mathbf Z}D(U_{\mathbf Z})$, the forgotten $\theta^G$ is the scalar transformation characterized by $\theta\alpha=Qb$ on every complex. The rank-one existential witness of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] can be chosen as this scalar row comparison on modules. With this choice the forgotten $\lambda^G$ equals that witness, and, for the mate $\beta^G:R\Gamma_H^G\to R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^GD(V)$ of [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting], forgetting $c_N^G=(\lambda_N^G)^{-1}\beta_N^G$ equals its scalar composite with derived restriction. These identifications preserve canonical shifts and boundaries. No uniqueness is asserted from a degree-zero normalization alone.

proof.text: First take $G=1$ and an injective $J$ in $\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z}(R)$. The rank-one case of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] supplies an isomorphism $\ell_J:Q[J\xrightarrow{T-1}J]\to R\Gamma_{R,\mathbf Z}(J[0])$. Its stated invariant-inclusion normalization says precisely $\ell_J Q(b_J)=\alpha_{\mathbf Z,J[0]}$. This computation unit is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], since $J[0]$ is bounded below and termwise injective. Hence $Q(b_J)$ is invertible. Equivalently $b_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism: applying the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $Q(b_J)$ gives exactly the cohomology maps of $b_J$. Thus the scalar injective row is proved from the statement of the lattice lemma, not from its proof or from any uniqueness of $\ell_J$.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived); rank-one invariant normalization in the cited lattice node.

proof.text: For injective $I$ in $\mathcal A_{G\times\mathbf Z}(R)$, [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting] makes $U_{\mathbf Z}I$ injective. The underlying invariant submodule is the scalar invariant submodule, by [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting]. Forgetting $G$ takes the row map to $b_{U_{\mathbf Z}I}$ literally: its coordinates are inclusion and zero, and $T-1$ is unchanged. Step 1 makes its image under $D(U_0)$ invertible. Conservativity of $D(U_0)$ makes $Q(b_I)$ invertible; the cohomology functors then show that the relative row is a quasi-isomorphism. For a bounded-below termwise injective complex $I$, let $A$ have rows $I^q\xrightarrow{T-1}I^q$ in cyclic degrees $0,1$, and let $B$ have $\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G I^q$ in cyclic degree $0$ and zero elsewhere, with vertical differential induced by $d_I$. The inclusions and zero components define $B\to A$: they commute with the vertical differential, and $(T-1)$ kills invariant sections. Its row maps are quasi-isomorphisms by the preceding argument. Shift the lower bound to zero and interchange indices using the signs of [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated]. The sign is one on the augmentation axis. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] to the exchanged double complexes. Their diagonals are finite; undoing the signed identifications gives exactly $b_I$, so $b_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), row variant; the cited signed-total node supplies index exchange and lower-bound translation.

proof.text: For every chain map $f:P\to P'$ the equality $K^G(f)b_P=b_{P'}\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(f)$ holds in both coordinates: the first is the naturality of invariant inclusion and the second is zero. The inclusion is the normalized invariant inclusion of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The functor $K^G$ respects homotopies and descends to $QK^G$ by [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated]. Thus $Qb$ is a natural transformation from $Q\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G$ to $QK^G Q$ on the bounded-below homotopy category. The source and target action categories are abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], with $v=\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G$ and target functor $QK^G$. It gives exactly one natural transformation $\theta^G$ with $\theta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,P}=Qb_P$ for every $P$. This is the required all-complex characterization.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05S7 (section-derived-functors); the universal property in the cited right-derived node.

proof.text:
On a bounded-below injective complex $I$, the characterization yields $\theta^G_{QI}=Qb_I(\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,I})^{-1}$, an isomorphism by step 2 and clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Every bounded-below complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to such an $I$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-subcategory-right-resolution-05T6] with the class of injective objects, using enough injectives from [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting]. Zero belongs to this class because every map to zero extends by the zero map; the cited resolution retains the chosen lower bound. Naturality along that quasi-isomorphism proves that every component of $\theta^G$ is invertible. Put $\lambda^G=(\theta^G)^{-1}$. For any specified quasi-isomorphism $a:N\to I$, naturality gives $Q(K^G a)\theta^G_{QN}=\theta^G_{QI}R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(Qa)$. Substituting the preceding formula and inverting gives precisely
$$\lambda^G_{QN}=(R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(Qa))^{-1}\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,I}Q(b_I)^{-1}Q(K^G a).$$
Every choice therefore gives the same arrow, the already defined $\lambda^G_{QN}$.

For a commuting diagram of specified injective resolutions, both $b$ and $K^G$ commute with its chain maps, and the normalized $R\Gamma$ comparisons commute by [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality]. Inverting the commuting isomorphisms in step 4 proves naturality on the entire diagram. For shifts, use the comparison $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^s y)$ of [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated]. On the image of $b$ its second coordinate is zero, so its square with the shifted augmentation commutes. On injective complexes, $\alpha$ is the normalized computation comparison; shifting an injective complex still computes the shifted derived functor. For cones, the cited resolution-naturality node makes the specified cone a bounded-below injective resolution and computes its comparison naturally. The cone isomorphism of the signed-total node is identity on the cyclic-degree-zero augmentation axis. Consequently the three augmentation squares commute, including the final arrow $-p$; its other summand has exactly the factor $(-1)^a$ prescribed there. The formulas for $\theta$ on injectives and step 4 now give shift and boundary compatibility for $\theta^G$ and its inverse. No unsigned total or degree-zero uniqueness is being substituted.

source.place: Tag 0156 (section-right-derived-functor), computation on cone resolutions; signed-total shift and cone formulas of the cited node.

proof.text:
Repeat steps 1--5 with $G=1$ to obtain the scalar $\theta$. Forgetting $G$ preserves injective complexes by [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting]. In the isomorphism $\delta_{\mathbf Z}$ of [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting], the computation units on those complexes are identical invariant inclusions. Both $U_0K^G=KU_{\mathbf Z}$ and $U_0b=bU_{\mathbf Z}$ are literal coordinate identities. Hence on every bounded-below injective $I$,
$$D(U_0)\theta^G_{QI}=Qb_{U_{\mathbf Z}I}(\alpha_{U_{\mathbf Z}I})^{-1}\delta_{\mathbf Z,QI}=\theta_{D(U_{\mathbf Z})QI}\delta_{\mathbf Z,QI}.$$
For any $P\to I$ as in step 4, naturality of $\delta$, of both $\theta$'s and of $K$ extends this equality to $QP$, since the resolution arrows are inverted. Inverting this equality identifies the forgotten $\lambda^G$ with the scalar $\lambda$. This uses the computation normalization on all injective complexes, not merely $H^0$ on modules.

source.place: Tag 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic); computation-unit-normalized forgetting comparison in the cited mate node.

proof.text:
The scalar $\lambda$ on modules has the invariant normalization: for $P[0]\to I$ the chain square $b_I\Gamma(a)=K(a)b_P$ and naturality of $\alpha$ give $\lambda_{QP}Qb_P=\alpha_P$. It is natural in $P$ by construction. It also satisfies the coefficient clause required of a rank-one witness in [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. Indeed let $s$ be scalar restriction along $R\to R'$ and resolve $P'$ by a bounded-below injective $I'$ over $R'$. Scalar restriction leaves abelian sheaves unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; kernels and sheafified cokernels are unchanged, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $b_{sI'}=s b_{I'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism even though $sI'$ need not be injective. Also $K_R(sI')=sK_{R'}(I')$ termwise. Since $\theta_R$ is invertible, $\theta_R\alpha_R=Qb$ implies that $\alpha_R(sI')$ is invertible. The canonical coefficient map is represented on this resolution by
$$R\Gamma_R(sP')\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Gamma_R(sI')=sQ\Gamma_{R'}(I')\xrightarrow{s\alpha_{R'}(I')}sR\Gamma_{R'}(P').$$
The first arrow is the inverse computation comparison. This is precisely the normalized derived coefficient comparison of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Substituting $\lambda=\alpha(Qb)^{-1}$ on these models makes its square with $\lambda_R, s\lambda_{R'}$ commute by cancellation. For $P\to sP'$ compose with naturality in $P$. We may therefore choose this natural scalar isomorphism as the rank-one existential witness; retain the existing witnesses for other ranks.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05S7 (section-derived-functors): acyclic computation of the canonical coefficient map; elementary cancellation on the two explicit row models.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting] identifies the forgotten $\beta^G$ with scalar derived restriction and identifies its shifts and boundaries. Step 6 identifies the forgotten $(\lambda^G)^{-1}$ with $\lambda^{-1}$ for the rank-one witness chosen in step 7. Applying the forgetting functor to $c_N^G=(\lambda_N^G)^{-1}\beta_N^G$ and preserving composition gives exactly the scalar composite. Both factors respect the shift and boundary comparisons by steps 5--6 and the cited mate statement, so their composite does too. The cases $G=1$, $H=1$, $u=0$, the zero complex and the zero ring introduce no exception: the same formulas reduce respectively to scalar formulas, identity restriction, $T-1=0$, or zero arrows. In particular no surjectivity of $T-1$ on an arbitrary module was asserted; step 1 only used injective modules.
